comparator.name: Chemistry (Scheikunde)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 Dutch Chemistry OER, ordinary route; prospective year pages are separately indicative 2027–2028
comparator.sourceNotes: External allocation rechecked 2026-10-08 against the adopted Dutch 2026–2027 OER, Articles 7.3–7.5 (pp.16–19). The Dutch regulation prevails over its translation and catalogue. The ordinary route totals 60 EC first-year requirements + 66 EC later requirements + 36 EC conditioned choice + 12 EC Bachelor Internship and Report + 6 EC genuinely free bachelor-level choice = 180 EC. Academic Writing in the Molecular Sciences is one 3-EC requirement. Writing about Science is not an additional universal requirement; Article 8.1 supplies replacement rules, and Article 7.4 separately permits nonoverlapping optional content. The 36-EC choice normally comprises Science-faculty bachelor courses with at least 12 EC from list BC1, or an approved minor subject to the remaining-space Chemistry minimum; it is not unrestricted open space. The previously selected RNA Structure and Function and Magnetic Resonance I (6 EC each) are retained as permitted BC1 instances. The remaining 24 EC is instantiated by the first six other distinct BC1 entries in formal list order: Advanced Molecular Biology 6, Applied Quantum Chemistry 3, Biophysical Chemistry 3, Catalysis 3, Chemical Biology Lab 3 and Chemometrics 6. This all-BC1 example satisfies the minimum without assuming a minor or optimizing against UCR. Minor exclusions in Article 7.7 remain applicable to other choices. List BC1 warns that not all options run every year; an actual timetable and enrolment must meet the catalogue requirements, and no availability guarantee is asserted. Year placement follows the indicative pages where consistent; formal Articles 7.4–7.5 govern the later-year aggregate, not a guaranteed entrant timetable. First-year Academic Skills at 0 EC is embedded in the later 3-EC Academic Skills requirement and is not added twice. PPO is embedded within credited courses. No formal named specialization is claimed. The original UCR assessment and checkedOn date remain unchanged; only its external credit description is corrected.

exception.reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 6 EC can be freely chosen and 36 EC is conditioned choice, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.
exception.curriculumContext: The adopted 2026–2027 Dutch OER establishes 60 first-year + 66 later compulsory + 36 conditioned choice + 12 independent research + 6 genuinely free EC = 180. The selected 36 EC is entirely drawn from BC1 and therefore exceeds the required minimum 12 EC Chemistry. Eight distinct choices are counted once; no magnetic-resonance alternatives or additional mandatory writing course are stacked. The prospective pages are indicative 2027–2028 context. This correction refreshes external facts only; the original UCR assessment dated 2026-09-25 remains pending stage-two reassessment.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, profile/topic enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biochemical content and molecular lab work, while HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 introduce life science and cells. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical/inorganic processes and recovery; ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST211 address materials life cycles and energy systems. DISGATE102, DISMATH211/214/314 and DISGATE101 provide some mathematical, statistical and programming support. None provides the laboratory and theory progression in chemical analysis, organic/inorganic synthesis, physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and quantum chemistry required to underpin this bachelor and its independent chemistry research internship. Isolated biochemical and environmental chemistry coverage cannot support a defensible 24-course Chemistry match.
